column1: # Planted blocks. NONE OF THESE IS A BLOCK FROM contents/ -- that is the point:
# a control drawn from the enumeration the instrument was built from cannot say
# whether the instrument works, only that it is consistent.
#   dotnet tools/blockcheck/bin/Release/net9.0/blockcheck.dll \
#       tools/blockcheck/plants tools/blockcheck/refs/bin/Release/net9.0/refs.txt
# Expected, and RE-RUN WHENEVER THE COMPILATION STRUCTURE IS TOUCHED:
#   Plant_Clean         BUILT    0
#   Plant_Missing       FAILED   1   CS0246
#   Plant_Unparseable   FAILED   5   CS1026,CS1513
#   Plant_Leak_A        BUILT    0
#   Plant_Leak_B        FAILED   1   CS0246      <-- the one that guards obligation 8
#   Plant_TopLevel      BUILT    0               <-- top-level statements, then a type
#   Plant_TopLevel_Bad  FAILED   1   CS8803      <-- the same two, in the other order
# Plant_Leak_B is the guard. It names a type declared by Plant_Leak_A, in a
# namespace they share, and it must NOT resolve: the two are different blocks.
# Put every block in one compilation and it resolves, and Plant_Leak_B comes
# back BUILT -- a false clean, with nothing in the output to say so. Measured
# The two TopLevel plants are phase 2's pair, and they are two-way in the sense
# that matters: the difference between them is LINE ORDER, not content. A block
# that puts its statements above its types is a Program.cs and must BUILD --
# which needs both the `toplevel` shape (or it is wrapped, and CS0116) and
# OutputKind.ConsoleApplication (or it is a library, and CS8805). Reverse the
# two halves and C# forbids it: CS8803, and the instrument must still say so.
# A rule that rescued both would be rescuing by shape rather than by grammar.
# id  page  ordinal  shape  n_usings  n_open  n_rest  scaffold
